findings.text: Directory entry creation helpers build symlink directory and mount point entries under a chosen parent and register them for later lookup. Symlink creation records destination length and keeps a private copy of the destination and associates link inode behavior. Directory creation supplies default read and execute access when no mode is given requests two links and associates directory file and inode behavior with optional forced lookup. Mount point creation uses directory type with read and execute access and leaves behavior pointers empty.

Convenience wrappers layer directory creation with progressively fewer arguments by fixing data to null or mode to zero or both while preserving the same underlying creation path. Single value file creation builds a regular entry then wires it to shared single show dispatch and stores caller show callback and data before registration.

Removal and small accessor helpers manage entry lifetime and metadata. Size setting stores a caller supplied length in the entry. Parent data access returns data stored in the parent of the entry for an inode. Single entry removal erases one name after translating a possibly nested path while subtree removal erases a whole hierarchy depth first. Both refuse permanent entries and then run rundown and release references.

Lookup readdir and inode helpers are exported for generic proc directories. Name lookup under a directory finds a child by name and instantiates an inode with dentry behavior selected by a force flag. Directory listing emits standard dot entries then children in tree order. Inode construction initializes a fresh inode from entry fields and selects file behavior by type and capability flags. Reference release frees the inode number and entry when the last reference drops.

File descriptor directory permission and operation tables are exported for use by higher layers. Permission for descriptor directories first tries generic access then allows members of the same thread group. Associated inode and file tables wire lookup permission attribute and size hooks for descriptor links and descriptor info files and directories.

Sequential file open and release wrappers with private state are exported. Open with a size allocates private state of that size together with supplied traversal callbacks and reports out of memory on failure. Release without private state delegates to shared release while release with private state frees the private area clears the pointer then delegates.

Descriptor directory members are named by decimal descriptor numbers. Lookup converts the name to an unsigned value and rejects unparsable names and descriptors without a live open file in the target task. Successful lookup passes the numeric value and observed open mode to an instantiation callback that builds the child.

Ownership and access mode for descriptor related inodes are refreshed from the target task on each validation and creation. Owner identifiers come from the dumping owner of the task and security state is synchronized to the inode. Link type inodes start as links and gain user read and execute when the open mode allows reading and gain user write and execute when the open mode allows writing. Info files keep regular file type and ignore open mode for permission bits.

Attribute handling keeps directory entry and inode consistent. Directory listing size for descriptor directories equals the number of currently open descriptors. Generic attribute fill provides other fields after link count is refreshed from the entry when the stored count is positive. Attribute change prepares and copies new attributes then writes owner group and mode back into the directory entry.

Inode construction from a directory entry follows a fixed order. Fresh inode receives caller data pointer low inode number and current timestamps and a back pointer to the entry. Empty entries become empty directories without further work. Otherwise mode ownership size and link count are copied only when the entry fields are nonzero. Regular files select iterating or plain file behavior based on capability flags with additional compat variants when supported. Directories receive stored directory behavior and links receive only inode behavior.

Process only mode disables generic name lookup and directory listing while leaving descriptor specific paths unaffected. Successful generic lookup chooses network style dentry behavior when the entry requests forced lookup and misc style otherwise. Link creation uses link type with broad access and directory creation without explicit mode uses read and execute access for all.

Sequential and single file helpers select private versus shared state by whether the entry advertises a nonzero state size. Sequential open and release use private variants when state is present and shared variants otherwise. Single open always binds the entry show callback and data to shared single state. Both operation sets use sequential read iteration and sequential seeking with matching release.
A dedicated header for descriptor helpers uses a standard include guard to prevent multiple inclusion within a single translation unit.

Child tree access is guarded by a dedicated read write lock. Lookup and directory listing hold read mode while locating first child skipping to the requested offset and stepping to successors. Mount directory and symlink creation and erasure during removal hold write mode. Listing takes an extra reference drops the lock across emission then retakes it to advance which keeps entries stable without holding the lock during output.

Descriptor state is read under task and read copy update protection. Counting open descriptors holds the task lock while sampling the file table under read copy update. Descriptor directory permission checks thread group membership under read copy update after generic permission fails. Mode sampling for a single descriptor uses task scoped file lookup with reference get and put around the read.

Entry teardown synchronizes with concurrent openers using a bias on a usage counter plus a completion and a dedicated unload spin lock. Rundown publishes a completion adds the bias and waits when prior users exist then repeatedly removes the first opener under the lock. Opener close marks closing outside the lock invokes the entry release hook then removes list linkage and wakes any waiter before freeing the opener record.

Directory entry lifetime uses reference counting with explicit get and put. Lookup and listing take a reference before dropping the tree lock and release it after finishing with the entry. Final put releases the allocated inode number then frees the entry. Erasure from the parent tree only unlinks and adjusts parent link count and does not itself drop the caller reference.

Descriptor instantiation carries a small record containing the numeric descriptor and the open mode observed at lookup or listing time. Lookup fills both fields before calling the type specific constructor while listing fills them per descriptor before emitting the name. Constructors copy the number into proc specific inode storage and use the mode for permission refresh.

Descriptor link and info objects use distinct but related operation sets. Link inodes use link inode behavior with a getter that resolves the path from the live file and a fixed small size. Info files use regular file inode behavior with access gated permission and sequential file operations for reading. Both share common dentry validation and deletion behavior and separate directory lookup iteration and attribute hooks.

Generic proc directories and files use a small family of operation tables. Directory inodes support lookup and attribute get and set while directory files support seek read and shared iteration. Plain files support only attribute setting at the inode layer. Misc dentries validate and delete based on usage sign while network dentries always request revalidation and deletion.

Proc operation sets for sequential and single files share iteration seeking and release shape but differ in open. Sequential set opens with entry sequence operations and optional private state size. Single set opens with entry single show callback and data. Global state includes a read write lock protecting the child tree and a slab cache for directory entries marked read only after init plus helpers to step between siblings in tree order.

Descriptor dentry validation moves among retry invalid and valid outcomes. Requests in read copy update context report retry without touching state. Requests with no task or no live file for the stored number report invalid so the dentry is dropped. Requests with a live file refresh ownership and mode from current task and file state then report valid.

Generic dentry lifetime has two policies selected at lookup. Misc entries stay valid while a usage indicator remains nonnegative and request revalidation and deletion once it turns negative. Network style entries unconditionally request revalidation and deletion on every check which forces fresh lookup each time.

Removal proceeds through translate locate erase rundown and release phases. Single removal erases one child then runs rundown and warns when the erased directory still has children. Subtree removal walks depth first erasing children before parents running rundown for each node after dropping the tree lock and releasing each reference. Permanent entries abort the walk with a warning and an error without erasing.

Descriptor and generic directory iteration share a position scheme where the first two positions represent dot entries and later positions index children. Listing starts by emitting dots then converts position to a child offset seeks to that child then emits one name per position increment. Descriptor listing resolves each candidate descriptor to a live file to capture mode before emission and stops cleanly when no further file exists or output fills.

Descriptor directory entry points consist of lookup and iteration pairs for links and info files. Each lookup delegates to a common helper with a type specific constructor. Each iteration delegates to a common directory reader with the same constructor. The constructors build unmountable spliced dentries with shared validation behavior and type specific inode and file hooks.

Generic directory entry points include lookup iteration permission and attribute operations. Lookup and iteration first enforce process only mode then delegate to helpers operating on the parent entry. Descriptor info permission requires ptrace style read access to the target task before generic permission. Descriptor directory permission falls back to thread group equality. Attribute hooks refresh link count or size and propagate changes back to the entry.

Sequential and single file entry points handle open and release for proc regular files. Sequential open chooses private or shared open based on advertised state size and sequential release mirrors that choice including freeing private state. Single open binds the entry callback and data to single state and releases with single release. Both use sequential iteration and seeking for data transfer.

Callers in read copy update context must handle retry from dentry validation without blocking. Missing tasks surface as search or missing entry errors depending on path while failed access checks surface as permission errors. Descriptor link resolution reports missing entry when the file is gone and permission helpers propagate generic access failures unless thread group membership allows access.

Removing permanent entries is forbidden and triggers a warning with no state change for single removal or an invalid argument result for subtree removal. Removing a directory that still contains children after erasure warns about leaking at least the first remaining child. Callers must also handle missing names during translation or lookup which yield warnings or missing entry errors.

Allocation and type errors have distinct handling. Failed inode allocation during lookup or instantiation yields missing entry or out of memory without leaking references. Failed destination duplication during symlink creation frees the partially built entry and returns null. Unknown inode types during construction hit a fatal trap rather than returning an error.

Descriptor iteration and counting must tolerate task exit and concurrent file table changes. Both report missing entry when the task cannot be resolved. Counting samples the open set under appropriate locking while iteration advances by descriptor number and skips to the next live file which avoids assumptions about density or stability of the table.
Dynamic proc inode numbers start at hex F0000000 which equals decimal 4026531840. Values at or above this boundary belong to dynamically allocated entries.

Descriptor link inodes advertise a fixed size of sixty four bytes with link type. Descriptor info files are created as regular files with read access for all. Symlink entries default to link type with broad access and directory entries default to directory type with read and execute access for all when no mode is supplied.
